page: Microsoft Azure D64lds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. The server is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage but does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64lds_v7 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 67973.49 and a PassMark CPU score of 83685.33. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2233.29. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 4705.01 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 311.23 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Data processing benchmarks show strong results, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 397.45 GB/sec and Redis SET operations processing 109.21 million operations per second. For LLM workloads, the server achieves strong prompt processing speeds of 214.92 tokens/sec on 7B models and 28.16 tokens/sec on 70B models.

The primary tradeoff of the D64lds_v7 is its low memory density relative to its high compute capacity, making it less suitable for memory-intensive applications. However, this configuration offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound workloads that require high-frequency processing and fast local storage without the overhead of excess RAM. The inclusion of a 3780 GB local NVMe SSD combined with strong database operation scores and high static web serving throughput makes this server suitable for high-throughput web serving, database operations, multi-threaded decompression, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
